images.title: A roti in fourth pieces
images.purpose: Set up the question: with fourth pieces of a roti as the unit, write a table by adding one fourth again and again.
images.composition: One whole roti cut into four on the left, and two loose pieces on the right with wide space between, and one question line below them.
images.exact_structure: Left: one round roti cut by two straight lines through the centre into 4 equal pieces, outlined grey #6B7280, all plain. Right: 2 loose pieces of exactly that size side by side, each filled teal #0072B2, with a grey plus sign between them. One question line under the 2 loose pieces. Exactly 1 roti, 4 equal pieces, 2 loose pieces.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any filled in table row or multiplication statement, or loose pieces of a different size from the roti's pieces
images.takeaway: Add one fourth again and again, and count how many.
images.description: A roti cut into 4 equal pieces beside 2 loose teal fourth pieces joined by a plus sign, under the question 1/4 + 1/4 = ?
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many fourth pieces are added and write that row of the table.

image_decisions.why: A roti in fourths beside two loose pieces sets up the table of fourths without writing any row.
